newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Austrian, Norwegian banks to issue Internet cash.
newsitem.headline: Austrian, Norwegian banks to issue Internet cash.

text.p: Norway and Austria's biggest banks, Den norske Bank and Bank Austria, will issue electronic cash developed by Digicash BV for use on the Internet, Dutch-based Digicash announced Monday.

DigiCash said the banks would issue its "ecash" product, which customers can use via a personal computer hooked up to the Internet to pay for a range of products and services, including database searches, news, entertainment and mail-order products.
Ecash is said to allow secure payments over the Internet using sophisticated encryption techniques that encode electronic cash payments.
The payment system, unlike existing credit card payment setups, allows for anonymous transactions as well as giving users the opportunity to make and receive payments.

"Ecash, like real cash, will allow consumers to shop in a secure and private manner which is both convenient and user-friendly. These ecash implementations will significantly stimulate the electronic commerce markets in both Austria and Norway," DigiCash said.
Recent licensees of the DigiCash product, Deutsche Bank and Advance Bank of Australia, are now in the final stages of implementing "ecash" and will soon be issuing it to their clients, DigiCash said.
